newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares boosted by economic data, BNI.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares boosted by economic data, BNI.

text.p: Jakarta shares ended higher on Wednesday as the latest economic data helped sentiment, which also received a boost from the Bank Negara Indonesia offering, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 3.47 points, or 0.59 percent, to close at 587.34 after touching a high of 588.46 points. Gainers led losers 73 to 34, with 51 counters unchanged.
Brokers said the market was likely to be mixed on Thursday, with a possibility of profit-taking following a 16.68 point rise in the index since last Friday.
"Some medium-sized issues are likely to see a further increase, but this could be dampened by local profit-taking," a foreign broker said.
Brokers said heavy demand for Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) offered stock which helped boost sentiment over the past three days was likely to continue, with a spin-off effect for some other banks.
BNI's four-day offering of 1.085 billion shares at 850 rupiah each ends on Thursday, ahead of its November 25 listing on the Jakarta and Surabaya exhanges.
"There is market talk that idle foreign funds are still in the market looking for alternative investments," said one foreign broker.
Shares of bank BDNI, Bank Bira and Bank Surya were actively traded. Brokers said investors unable to secure as much BNI stock as they wanted were looking at other banking counters.
BDNI topped the active list with 7.2 million shares traded, rising 125 rupiah to 1,825 rupiah. Brokers also attributed the rise to good fundamentals and the feeling that the prevaling price was low.
Telecommunication heavyweight Telkom rose 50 rupiah to 3,800 on a volume of about three million shares, an increase brokers said was in line with its rise in New York on Tuesday.
Satellite and international telephone operator Indosat rose 25 rupiah to 7,325 on a turnover of 518,000 shares following its nine-month results.
Indosat posted a net income of 361.6 billion rupiah for the first nine months of the year, a rise of 5.5 percent over the same 1995 period.
Brokers said the increase was slightly below expectations but they were generally happy with the result. They said the full reaction would be seen on Thursday.
